summary: Dorchester County, Maryland, 120-foot state fire tower built 1937 near East New Market; first with short-wave radio in 1939; listed as gone, removal undated.

facts.design: 120-foot tower on four cement piers, with a pointed-top observation room and fire table
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal date in the sources read

events.note: 120-foot structure on the Samuel Webster farm between East New Market and Shiloh, built by CCC crews from the Snow Hill camp; ready for use August 1, 1937 per a July 30 report
Towerman Charles Mosely stationed at Shiloh; tower opened as the spring fire season began
Short-wave radio installed; the Daily Times called Shiloh the first tower equipped with short wave radio; site chosen as central for Caroline, Dorchester and Talbot counties

evidence.supports: built 1937 by CCC men from the Snow Hill camp on the Samuel Webster farm
evidence.quote: The 120-foot structure is being erected on the Samuel Webster farm by CCC men from the Snow Hill camp housed at the Vienna camp while the tower is being built.

evidence.supports: tower constructed by International Derrick Company, set on cement piers, four foundation blocks of 7 to 8 tons
evidence.quote: the tower which is being constructed by the International Derrick Company is set on cement piers, the four foundation blocks weighing from 7 to 8 tons each.

evidence.supports: pointed-top observation room with fire table (July 12 report: table 'will be furnished' with a map)
evidence.quote: The fire table in the pointed-top observation room will be furnished with a map

evidence.supports: fire table covers a 15-mile radius (July 12 report)
evidence.quote: to enable the towerman to sight fires in a radius of 15 miles of the tower

evidence.supports: fire map covers a 16-mile area (July 30 report)
evidence.quote: a fire map covering a 16-mile area

evidence.supports: between East New Market and Shiloh, late-August completion expected (July 12 report)
evidence.quote: a fire tower between East New Market and Shiloh the latter part of August

evidence.supports: second tower built in Dorchester County (July 30 report)
evidence.quote: the second one built in Dorchester County

evidence.supports: built by the State Department of Forestry (July 30 report)
evidence.quote: built on the Eastern Shore by the State Department of Forestry

evidence.quote: The Shiloh tower, the first to be equipped with short wave radio, opened yesterday as the spring fire season began officially.

evidence.supports: listed as Tower, Gone, Dorchester County, coordinates

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 12, 1937 report gives a 15-mile radius for the fire table; the July 30, 1937 report gives a 16-mile area for the fire map. The story reports both figures.
A July 12, 1937 report expected completion in the latter part of August; a July 30 report said the tower would be ready for use on August 1. The story uses the July 30 date as the ready date.

notes_for_editor: Built, staffing and 1939 radio rest on one page of 1937 to 1939 newspaper excerpts transcribed by the Forest Lookouts site; the original clippings were not read. Fate after 1939 is not in any source read: the only status is the FFLA 'Tower Gone' row, with no removal date or cause. The 2007 DNR Forestry Towers resource document does not mention Shiloh. A DNR poster surfaced in search (tower 33, 1939, 120 ft, CCC) could not be fetched (404) and is not cited. Lead for removal date: Barbara Garner, A View from the Top, Maryland's Fire Towers (Abecedarian Books, 2012).
